paths.name: Kubernetes Roadmap
paths.description: The complete free Kubernetes roadmap, from your first pod to operators, storage, troubleshooting, and production operations. Built from our own course, workshops, articles, and labs.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.outcome: Explain to a colleague what the control plane does, and why pods (not containers) are the unit of scheduling.
stages.mission: Draw the architecture from memory: API server, etcd, scheduler, kubelet, and what talks to what.
stages.intro: Everything else builds on a mental model of the control plane. Start here even if you have used kubectl before.

stages.title: Run it locally

steps.title: On a Mac? KIAC: Kubernetes in Apple Containers
The real thing: kubeadm + containerd + Cilium

stages.outcome: Spin up and destroy multi-node clusters without fear.
stages.mission: Create a 3-node cluster, kill a node, and watch what happens to its pods.
stages.intro: Theory sticks when you break things. Get a cluster you can destroy without fear.

stages.title: Workloads & services

steps.title: Services: all 5 types, how they actually work
EndpointSlices: why Endpoints had to die
Ingress and the Gateway API era (with a real migration)
Autoscaling: HPA, VPA, KEDA, and when each applies
Progressive delivery: rolling, blue-green, and canary releases
Cluster essentials: cert-manager, external-dns, and the add-ons every cluster runs

stages.outcome: Deploy a stateful app with services in front and explain the full traffic path.
stages.mission: Deploy an app plus a database, expose it via ClusterIP, NodePort, and Ingress, and explain the difference.
stages.intro: Now that you have a cluster, learn how apps actually run on it and how traffic reaches them.

stages.title: Internals
stages.outcome: Answer 'what happens when I kubectl apply' end to end, from API server to running container.
stages.mission: Follow one pod from apply to Running: watch the events, the scheduler decision, and the kubelet start.
stages.intro: You can use Kubernetes; now learn what it does under the hood, because that is what debugging demands.

stages.title: Storage & secrets

steps.title: Secrets with the Secrets Store CSI Driver (video)
CSI from scratch: how volumes really attach (article)

stages.outcome: Choose the right secrets approach for a team and defend the choice.
stages.mission: Wire External Secrets or Sealed Secrets into a demo app end to end.
stages.intro: Stateless is easy. Real systems have state and credentials, and this is where clusters get hurt.

stages.title: Operators & CRDs
stages.outcome: Read any operator's CRDs and predict what its reconcile loop will do.
stages.mission: Build a tiny operator with Kubebuilder that labels namespaces, and break its reconcile loop on purpose.
stages.intro: Kubernetes' real power is extending the API itself. This is how the ecosystem you use every day is built.

stages.title: Security

steps.title: Policy as code in 2026: Kyverno and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy

stages.outcome: Harden a cluster with RBAC, network policies, and admission control, and know which audit logs matter.
stages.mission: Lock down a namespace so a compromised pod can reach nothing except its own database.
stages.intro: With workloads running, lock them down. Everything here comes up in real audits and real incidents.

stages.title: Production operations

steps.title: Requests, limits, and cost: from monitoring to automation
Multi-tenancy in 2025 and beyond: namespaces, virtual clusters, and hard isolation
Day-2 ops from a control room (SRELens)
Written troubleshooting playbook: common failures, fast diagnosis
Multi-cluster and cell-based architectures: how large platforms scale
Backup and disaster recovery that actually restores

stages.outcome: Debug a broken cluster under pressure and upgrade one without downtime.
stages.mission: Break your local cluster on purpose (kill etcd, wedge a node) and recover it.
stages.intro: The final stretch: keeping clusters alive under pressure. Upgrades, observability, chaos, and 3am debugging.

paths.name: Docker & Containers Roadmap
paths.description: Containers from first principles: what docker run actually does, how images become a supply chain, networking, Compose, and modern image building. Workshop, video series, and deep-dive articles.

stages.title: First principles

steps.title: Day 1: what happens when you type docker run
How containers work behind the scenes

stages.outcome: Explain what a container actually is: namespaces, cgroups, and a tarball.
stages.mission: Explain docker run flag by flag, or run a container with unshare and chroot, no Docker.
stages.intro: A container is not a VM. Understand the primitives and everything else stops being magic.

stages.title: Images done right

steps.title: Your images are a supply chain (and it's probably broken)
BuildKit and buildx: the secret gems

stages.outcome: Cut an image in half and know exactly what is inside everything you ship.
stages.mission: Take any real Dockerfile and reduce the final image size by 50% with multi-stage builds.
stages.intro: Your image is your supply chain. Learn to build small, fast, and verifiable.

stages.title: Networking & state

steps.title: Volumes, networks, and the real world

stages.outcome: Debug 'container cannot reach X' methodically instead of restarting things.
stages.mission: Connect two containers across a user-defined network and trace how the packets flow.
stages.intro: Containers are isolated until they need to talk and remember things. This is where most confusion lives.

stages.title: Multi-container & beyond

steps.title: Compose: how Docker actually gets used
Ship it, and what comes next
Runtime security: capabilities, seccomp, and what containers can really do
From Compose to Kubernetes: migration guide

stages.outcome: Compose a full stack, and recognize the moment you have outgrown Compose.
stages.mission: Ship a 3-service app with Compose, then write down what would break at scale.
stages.intro: Real apps are several containers. Compose them, ship them, and know when to graduate to Kubernetes.

paths.name: DevOps Roadmap
paths.description: The free DevOps roadmap people actually finish: Linux, Git, networking, CI/CD, GitOps, IaC, monitoring, and platform engineering, in the right order. Videos and articles from our own catalog.

stages.title: The ground floor
stages.outcome: Live in a terminal: navigate, script, and debug basic networking without copy-paste.
stages.mission: Write a shell script that health-checks a service and alerts when it goes down.
stages.intro: Every tool later in this path assumes you are comfortable in a terminal. Build that comfort first.

stages.title: Version control & automation
stages.outcome: Ship code through a pipeline you built yourself.
stages.mission: Build a GitHub Actions pipeline that tests, builds, and pushes an image on every commit.
stages.intro: Git is the center of everything modern delivery does. Automate around it.

stages.title: Infrastructure as code

steps.title: Secrets management: getting started with Vault

stages.outcome: Recreate your entire environment from a git repo, on purpose, twice.
stages.mission: Provision and destroy a full environment twice; the second time should be boring.
stages.intro: Clicking through consoles does not scale and does not repeat. Make infrastructure a git repo.

stages.title: GitOps & Kubernetes

steps.title: GitOps with Argo CD: complete hands-on workshop

stages.outcome: Explain why git is the source of truth and make a cluster converge to it.
stages.mission: Set up Argo CD to deploy an app, then break the live state and watch it heal itself.
stages.intro: Combine the last two stages: git becomes the source of truth for what runs in the cluster.

stages.title: Observe & platform

steps.title: Kubernetes Observability 101: metrics, logs, dashboards, traces (workshop)
SRE fundamentals: SLOs, error budgets, on-call
Build an internal developer platform: golden paths and Backstage

stages.outcome: Answer 'is it healthy?' with dashboards and SLOs, not vibes.
stages.mission: Instrument one service end to end: metrics, logs, one dashboard, and one alert that actually matters.
stages.intro: Shipping is half the job. Now measure it, and pave the road so others ship faster.

paths.name: AI Infrastructure Roadmap
paths.description: LLMs and GPUs the way production runs them: local inference foundations, GPU sharing, the MLOps stack real platforms are built on (Kubeflow, KServe, batch scheduling), and LLMOps/AIOps for day 2.

stages.title: Local LLM foundations

steps.title: Quantization demystified: BF16 to NVFP4 to GGUF
Inference engines: vLLM, llama.cpp, and what to pick
Docker Model Runner: local AI app, no API keys (video)

stages.outcome: Run a model locally and explain tokens per second, quantization, and the memory math.
stages.mission: Run the same model at two quantization levels and measure the speed and quality difference.
stages.intro: Before Kubernetes, GPUs, or platforms: understand how inference actually works on hardware you control.

stages.title: GPUs on Kubernetes

steps.title: Slicing GPUs with NVIDIA MIG (includes GPU Operator)

stages.outcome: Share one GPU across workloads and defend your strategy: MIG vs time-slicing vs HAMi.
stages.mission: Slice a GPU with MIG (or simulate with HAMi) and run two isolated workloads on it.
stages.intro: GPUs are the scarcest resource in the building. Learn to share them without wasting them.

stages.title: Training & MLOps platform

steps.title: Why ML needs a platform: notebooks, pipelines, and experiment tracking
Batch scheduling: gang scheduling and the Workload API (Kubernetes 1.35 demo)
Kueue: queues, quotas, and fair sharing for training jobs
Argo Workflows: pipelines and batch orchestration on Kubernetes
Kubeflow in 2026: what it is now and when to use it
Model registries and versioning in practice

stages.outcome: Stand up a real ML platform: notebooks, pipelines, tuning, and batch scheduling with quotas.
stages.mission: Run one training pipeline end to end: train a small model, tune one hyperparameter, and version the result.
stages.intro: One model on one GPU is a demo. Teams need notebooks, pipelines, tuning, and fair scheduling: a platform.

stages.title: Serving & inference in production

steps.title: Serving fundamentals: engines, batching, and OpenAI-compatible APIs (from our local LLM series)
From laptop to cluster: what changes when serving moves to Kubernetes
vLLM on Kubernetes: production serving deep dive
KServe: standardized inference endpoints and when you need them
Scaling inference: autoscaling, caching, and cost per token

stages.outcome: Serve a model behind a real endpoint and defend your runtime choice (vLLM, Triton, ONNX) like production teams do.
stages.mission: Deploy one model two ways: a standardized serving stack and a raw vLLM deployment; compare latency and ops burden.
stages.intro: Training gets the glory; serving pays the bills. Put models behind reliable, scalable endpoints.

stages.title: LLMOps, AIOps & agents

steps.title: K8sGPT: AIOps, when Kubernetes meets AI
LLMOps: evals, prompt versioning, and safe rollouts
RAG infrastructure: vector databases on Kubernetes
Model and drift monitoring in production

stages.outcome: Run models and agents in production with observability, cost control, and memory hygiene.
stages.mission: Put an agent behind a gateway, cap its spend, audit what it remembers, and let K8sGPT explain your next cluster incident.
stages.intro: Day 2: costs, observability, memory, and letting AI help run the infrastructure itself.
